change.title: pr-7
change.description: scale-color $lightness must use $secondary for dark themes
change.author: Jeff Atwood

findings.title: Light-theme colour of reply-to author link changed from 30% to 70%
findings.body: `dark-light-choose` returns its first argument for light themes (`common/foundation/variables.scss:46-48`). The old value here was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`, and the new light argument is `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`. In light themes the `.topic-meta-data h5 a` link is therefore much lighter and has less contrast. The PR only aims to add a dark-theme variant. The light value should stay at 30%, with the dark value mirrored to `scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%)`.

findings.title: Group member name colour changed in light theme (30% → 50%)
findings.body: The original was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The new light argument is `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%)`, and the dark argument is also 50%. The light-theme `.group-member-info .name` therefore gets lighter and loses its distinction from `.title`, which is 50% and sits just below it. Use `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`.

findings.title: Group member name colour changed in light theme (30% → 50%)
findings.body: This is the same regression as in `desktop/user.scss`. The original light value was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. It is now 50%, so `.name` is the same colour as `.title` in light themes. Use 30% for the light argument and `scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%)` for the dark argument.

findings.title: `.custom-message-length` light value changed from 70% to 30% and the pair is inverted
findings.body: The original was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`, a faint hint colour. The new light argument is `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`, so the light theme gets a much darker colour. The dark argument is `$secondary 70%`. The desktop equivalent (`desktop/modal.scss:94`) correctly uses primary 70% / secondary 30%. Use `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`.

findings.title: Mobile `h3` colour changed in light theme (20% → 50%)
findings.body: The original was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)`. The new value is `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. The light-theme heading therefore gets much lighter. The desktop counterpart (`desktop/topic-post.scss:321`) uses 20% / 80%. Use `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 80%))`.

contracts.action: Wrap hard-coded scale-color($primary, ...) colours in dark-light-choose with a $secondary-based dark variant across 32 stylesheets
contracts.equivalent_path: Existing usages of dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary,...), scale-color($secondary,...)) e.g. desktop/topic-post.scss:84
contracts.before_after: Before: one colour computed from $primary for all themes. After: the light theme should get the same value as before and the dark theme the mirrored $secondary value. Five sites (desktop/topic-post.scss:291, desktop/user.scss:522, mobile/user.scss:497, mobile/modal.scss:102, mobile/topic-post.scss:182) change the light value as well.
contracts.visible_effect: Colours of text, icons and borders are chosen at SCSS compile time by comparing brightness($primary) to brightness($secondary). Light themes visibly change at the five sites above.
contracts.failure_mode: No runtime failure. The wrong light-theme colour is shown silently.

summary: The PR wraps hard-coded `scale-color($primary, …)` colours in `dark-light-choose` so dark themes use `$secondary`. Most sites keep the original light value and mirror it for dark (`primary N%` / `secondary (100−N)%`). Five sites change the light-theme value as well, which the PR title doesn't describe: `desktop/topic-post.scss:291`, `desktop/user.scss:522`, `mobile/user.scss:497`, `mobile/modal.scss:102` and `mobile/topic-post.scss:182`. I read only the SCSS and the `dark-light-choose` definition, so I did not check how any of the changed colours render.
